title: Linear-growth conjecture for Split Smallest and Combine Smallest games
source: Ruoci Li, Xiaonan Li, Steven J. Miller, Clayton Mizgerd, Chenyang Sun, Dong Xia and Zhyi Zhou, “Deterministic Zeckendorf Games”, arXiv:2006.16457 (2020). (https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.16457); Conjecture 1.4 and the strategy priorities are in Li et al., arXiv:2006.16457

lanes.manuscript_rereview: zeckendorf-347063-manuscript-rereview-opus-20261118-r1/REVIEW.md (Claude Opus 5.5, PASS WITH EDITORIAL EDITS; revised copy used)

significance.root_decision: Source-bound resolution of the Combine Smallest half of Conjecture 1.4 for the deterministic Zeckendorf game started from n copies of F_1: the number of moves is CS(n) = c n + O(sqrt(n) log n) with c = 5/2 - phi + sum_{j>=2} 1/F_{2j} = 1.2064811686..., with an explicit error constant. The Split Smallest half (constant phi^2) is due to Cusenza et al. and is only attributed. The MathDB record states the start position as the Zeckendorf decomposition of n, which gives zero moves and makes the record trivially false as literally written; the result proves the statement with the source start position.
significance.caveat: Record defect: the MathDB start position differs from the source; accepted on the source statement by root judgment (held for a user ruling since 2026-11-09; user may overrule). Significance modest. The proved error term is far from sharp (numerically the error stays under about 20 up to n = 3*10^7).

root_basis: Root extracted all 20 modules from the appendix into an empty directory, rebuilt and kernel-checked them (all exit 0, object hashes identical to the audited build, axioms exactly the allowed three). Statement fidelity against the source was established by the independent Lean audit of 2026-11-09 and re-confirmed by the manuscript re-review. The written proof failed a first independent review, was rewritten, and passed an independent re-review with its own simulator (1.3 million table instances).
